post.caption:
Almost all seaborne trade funnels through roughly six chokepoints: Suez, Panama, Malacca, Hormuz, Bab-el-Mandeb and the Danish straits. Around a fifth of container traffic passes Malacca and around a fifth of all oil passes Hormuz. Efficiency created the fragility: just-in-time supply chains hold almost no reserve, so a single blockage propagates worldwide within days. One ship sideways in Suez was the demonstration.
